title.narrative: UNODC FishNET 2.0 Capacity to address crimes in the fisheries sector

description.narrative:
This project aims to support developing countries to address crimes in the fisheries sector, and corruption linked to these crimes. With fish stocks rapidly being depleted, entire aquatic ecosystems are suffering from disruptions in the food chain and habitat degradation, crimes in the fisheries sector negatively impact life below water while corroding human and economic security. The project builds on the work of FishNET I, in particular efforts to increase the understanding of crimes in the fisheries sector globally, the resource guides prepared for this purpose, and the capacity building activities undertaken to date. Priority countries are Benin, Ghana, Kenya, Namibia, São Tomé und Príncipe, South Africa, Somalia, Tanzania, Togo and Vietnam. Given the underrepresentation of women in customs and law enforcement in particular, gender mainstreaming is a priority.
Outcome 1: Legal and policy frameworks to address crimes in the fisheries sector are strengthened Outcome 2: Criminal justice and law enforcement capacity to respond to crimes in the fisheries value chain is enhanced Outcome 3: Capacity to address corruption in the fisheries sector is strengthened Outcome 4: Awareness on the serious nature of crimes in the fisheries sector raised at both regional and international levels Outcome 5: Network of qualified women strengthened
